summary.root_cause_text: Deploy v1.6 (payments client HTTP library upgrade) fails with 'Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable', so orders were processed without payment.
recommended: Fix Decimal serialization in the payments client before redeploying the HTTP library upgrade
Add a payment-failure alert at WARNING or ERROR level instead of DEBUG

events.text:
version: v1.6
payment_provider_url: internal://payments-v1
queue_max: 1000
worker_count: 1
sync_interval_s: 5
v1.6 deploy broke payments. Rollback first.
Rolled back version v1.6 -> v1.3. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).

root_causes: Deploy v1.6 (payments client HTTP library upgrade) fails with 'Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable', so orders were processed without payment.
evidence: DEBUG payment: provider call failed: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable (orders 18-36)
config reloaded version v1.3 -> v1.6 at 06:29:23, just before failures
args.impact: Orders created after v1.6 went live were processed without payment: 10 unpaid at alert time (SAR 1987.05, USD 745.3, total_sar 4781.93). The failures kept growing until rollback. Reprocessing then paid 26 orders (money_recovered total_sar 11623.32). No ledger integrity failures.
recommended_actions: Fix Decimal serialization in the payments client before redeploying the HTTP library upgrade
Add a payment-failure alert at WARNING or ERROR level instead of DEBUG
args.summary: Deploy v1.6 broke payment calls with a Decimal JSON serialization error. Orders were marked processed without payment, and /health stayed green. I rolled back to v1.3 and reprocessed all unpaid orders. All invariants are green again.
